title: Chapter 2 — Nelson Mandela + A Tiger in the Zoo (Class 10 CBSE English)
subject: English
chapter_title: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom

slides.title: Nelson Mandela / A Tiger in the Zoo
What you'll be able to do
bullets: Discuss Mandela's ideas on courage, love, freedom.
Connect both pieces — meditation on freedom.

slides.title: Mandela's Inauguration
bullets: First BLACK President of South Africa.
World leaders, daughter Zenani, deputies de Klerk + Mbeki.

slides.title: Symbols of the new nation
bullets: Once a CRIME for Mandela to sing it!
South African Air Force fly-past in new colours.

slides.title: Apartheid — short background
bullets: Black Africans denied vote, education, equal jobs.
Forced to carry passes, removed to 'homelands'.

slides.title: Mandela's life — timeline
bullets: 27 YEARS in prison; mostly Robben Island.

slides.title: Mandela's key ideas — twin obligations
bullets: Free society: BOTH can be fulfilled.

slides.title: Mandela on courage and love
bullets: Courage = TRIUMPH OVER fear, not absence of it.
Brave man CONQUERS fear, not denies it.
If they can learn to hate, they can be TAUGHT to love.

slides.title: Three stages of freedom
bullets: BOY in Transkei: freedom = run, swim, plough, walk village.
YOUNG MAN in Joburg: freedom = dignity, marry, work.
No one is free until ALL are free.
OPPRESSOR is as unfree as oppressed.

slides.title: The 'long walk'
bullets: Some way walked; long climb still to come.
Freedom = not just casting off chains.
Living in a way that ENHANCES others' freedom.

slides.title: A Tiger in the Zoo — by Leslie Norris
bullets: Subject: a tiger in a zoo.

slides.title: Alternating stanzas — caged + wild
bullets: Stanza 1 — caged: paces on pads of velvet.
Stanza 2 — wild: slides through long grass, lurks near water-hole.
Stanza 4 — wild: snarls near a village, terrorises.
Stanza 5 — caged at night: stares at brilliant stars.

slides.title: What the poem shows
bullets: Tiger keeps DIGNITY (ignores visitors, paces with care).
Loses environment, hunting power, fear-inducing presence.

slides.title: Connection — Mandela + Tiger
bullets: Mandela: oppressor is as unfree as oppressed.
Tiger: cage diminishes both creature AND keeper.

slides.title: Three iconic Mandela quotes
bullets: 'Apartheid created a deep and lasting wound.'
'No one is truly free if all are not free.'
'Love comes more naturally to the human heart than its opposite.'

slides.title: You try (5 min)
bullets: 2. Why is courage the 'triumph over fear'?
3. Three contrasts in 'A Tiger in the Zoo'.
4. Why are the two pieces paired?
5. What does 'oppressor as unfree as oppressed' mean?

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Mandela inaugurated 10 May 1994 — end of apartheid.
27 years in prison; first black President.
Twin obligations; courage = triumph over fear; love over hate.
No one free until all are free.
Norris's poem — caged + wild scenes alternated.
Both pieces — meditation on freedom at every scale.
